messages:
jen: Heads-up — seeing flaky `apply` failures when infra PRs merge. GH Actions runs matrix jobs, Atlantis sometimes tries to apply the same workspace concurrently and one of the applies fails with a lock/timeout. Anyone seen this pattern recently?
kevin: Yep saw this yesterday morning. Looks like our S3-backed Atlantis lock occasionally isn't persisted between short-lived gha runners (race on creating the lock file).
sachin: A couple options: (1) upload plan artifacts + single 'apply' job that pulls artifact and runs atlantis apply, or (2) enforce a per-branch concurrency group so only one runner handles infra for a branch. Also add an argocd wait step after apply so the pipeline doesn't finish until manifests are observed.
jen: I like the artifact + single apply approach. Can you sketch the GH action step for upload?
sachin: Sure — example snippet:```yaml
- name: Upload terraform plan
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: tf-plan-${{ github.sha }}
    path: ./plan.out

# later in apply job
- name: Download plan
  uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: tf-plan-${{ github.sha }}
```
jen: Alternatively we could gate the merge with a label-based apply: only run apply when someone adds `apply` label. That avoids accidental concurrent applies from multiple workflows.
kevin: We already use `concurrency` but matrix jobs generate different groups. You can use a single group key to serialize across the matrix, e.g.:```yaml
concurrency:
  group: infra-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
```
atlantis-bot: Atlantis: Lock acquired for workspace "prod" by PR #824 (apply queued) :lock:
deploy-bot: ArgoCD: Started sync for app `infra` from commit `b7f9a2c` — watching for health/events
jen: One more wrinkle — secret bootstrap. Sometimes ArgoCD sees manifests before sealed-secrets / sops keys are available and the secret objects don't get created, causing the app to go degraded. We need to ensure decryption happens in the runner (or use sealed secret operator) before finishing apply.
sachin: Good catch. Plan: 1) upload plan artifact, 2) single gated apply job triggered by label, 3) post-apply wait-step that polls argocd for healthy status (with a timeout & retry/backoff). On timeout, dump `kubectl get events -n infra` and `kubectl get pods -n infra -o wide`.
kevin: SGTM. Add a 5m exponential backoff for argocd wait and fallback to manual rollback on timeout. Also add a short log-collection step:```bash
kubectl get events -n infra --sort-by=.lastTimestamp
kubectl describe pods -n infra | sed -n '1,200p'
```
jen: I'll put together a PR with the workflow changes tonight and link it here. If folks can review + test on staging tomorrow that'd be great. @kevin @sachin please lmk if you want a different approach. :thumbsup:
kevin: Looking good. Quick q: should apply job run on the same runner image that has sops installed? If yes, add sops to the job image or install via step.
sachin: Yes — add `sops` or use a small bootstrap step to `pip install sops` / use the `mozilla/sops` image. I'll add that to the draft.
jen: Thanks — will update the PR with the apply gating + argocd wait hooks.
sachin: :+1:
